if the autoSystemTime is False the mothbox will get set to whatever value you put here ONE time and then disable manual time setting (to prevent Groundhog Days) until you set AutosystemTime to False again
how long each capture window lasts (in minutes): the lights and camera run this long each time. Capture windows that touch or overlap the next one just keep going
add or remove days 1-7 for monday through sunday
specify what hour you want things to turn on in 24 timeframe separate multi values with a semicolon
specify a specific minute that the schedule will start
not currently used by the mothbox
nominal voltage of the battery (voltage is says on the battery like 12v or 24 v)
this is the watt-hours of power the battery is rated for - for talentcell pb1202b it is 142 - if your battery only have amp-hours you can multiply Ah by the voltage to get watt hours
this is the voltage of the battery when its about 80 percent full (This helps you calibrate the overal battery percent meter for different batteries)
this is the voltage of the battery when it is about 20 percent full
write an SSID of a wifi you want to add to the pi
write the wifi password (not currently implemented)
time in minutes between each photo. Default is 2 minutes
auto detects a Mothbox Pro PCB or a DIY relay build at boot. Set to pro or diy to force it if detection ever guesses wrong
time in minutes between backups of new photos to the USB drive. Default is 5 (valid 1-999). A final backup always runs at the end of every capture window regardless

the clock coin cell: regular (CR2032 - never charged) or rechargeable (ML2020/ML2032 - charged). Must match the cell in the box: charging a regular cell can make it leak and an uncharged rechargeable one runs down
True runs the box in HI POWER (wifi on - never sleeps) whenever the Active switch is on - like a Pro with its HI switch on. For a Mothbox DIY which has no HI switch. Uses much more battery
True uploads new photos to the server below (with rclone). Only in HI POWER mode - and needs wifi or another internet connection
cloud upload: how to connect: sftp - ftps - ftp - webdav - s3 - or rclone_conf (uses rclone.conf next to this file). Stored as plain text
cloud upload: the server (sftp/ftps/ftp: host name; webdav: full https address; s3: endpoint - blank for AWS). Stored as plain text
cloud upload: folder on the server (s3: bucket/folder; rclone_conf: optionally remote:folder). Stored as plain text
cloud upload: S3 region if it needs one. Stored as plain text
cloud upload: user name (sftp/ftps/ftp/webdav). Stored as plain text
cloud upload: password (sftp/ftps/ftp/webdav). Stored as plain text: anyone with the SD card can read it - so use a sub-account limited to one folder
cloud upload: S3 access key ID. Stored as plain text
cloud upload: S3 secret access key. Stored as plain text
cloud upload: between_windows (default: while the box waits dark between capture windows) or anytime
cloud upload: minutes between upload attempts (10-1440). One also starts when each capture window ends
cloud upload: optional speed limit e.g. 2M (megabytes per second). Blank for none
